subjects.name: Nathan's Famous Hot Dog Eating Contest

summary: PR man George Shea turned the Nathan's Hot Dog Eating Contest on Coney Island into a televised sport through Major League Eating, using invented myths, jingoism against Japanese champion Takeru Kobayashi and a sidelined women's division to win publicity.
keywords: The Good, the Bad, the Hungry (30 for 30)

evidence.note: Shea born in Boston around 1964-65, brothers raised in Maine
segment on ad man Morty Matz, who invented the contest in the early 1970s and its fake origin myths
Shea takes over the Nathan's account and contest around the early 1990s
Belt of Fat hoax and other publicity stunts built on invented claims
after 2007 the Sheas stoke anti-Japanese crowd hostility toward Kobayashi
Kobayashi held to an exclusive contract, refuses to compete, arrested on stage in 2010
women split into a separate division with less airtime and prize money; Sonya Thomas pressured
Shea still hosting the contest at release; Cameo video from 2021

notes: Reverse episode hosted by Jamie Loftus. Shea's birth year given as 1964 or 1965 (1964 used, approximate). Takeover year and Kobayashi arrest year are blanked in the transcript; early 1990s and 2010 from general knowledge. misogyny-manosphere is the closest fit for the gender-segregated women's division; there is no theme for workplace sex discrimination. Richard Shea is co-founder but has no segment of his own.
